title: Ketamine in WWOX-related epilepsy
summary: Ketamine remains a research hypothesis for WWOX-related epilepsy. The reviewed sources do not establish benefit in WWOX-DEE, either for an acute episode or for ongoing seizure control. The reviewed pediatric evidence also leaves functional improvement at 6–8 weeks after brief peri-intubation ketamine undetermined.
evidence: Breton et al. reported that the competitive NMDA receptor antagonist d-APV stopped spontaneous bursts in cortical slices from mice with neuron-specific Wwox loss. Ketamine was not tested in those slices.
Paediatric studies of ketamine in status epilepticus cover other or mixed causes.
limits: No controlled ketamine result was found in a WWOX-deficient system. A slice result would leave developmental benefit, ongoing seizure control and safety in infants unresolved.

graph.evidence: d-APV stopped bursts in slices after neuronal Wwox loss.
graph.inference: NMDA receptors contribute to bursts in this preparation.
graph.hypothesis: Pore blockade may reproduce the effect.

inference: The slice result supports a contribution of NMDA receptor signalling to bursts in that preparation. Ketamine blocks the channel pore and its effect can depend on the state of the circuit.
hypothesis: A pore blocker may suppress Wwox-related bursts when its effect on NMDA receptor activity is comparable to that of d-APV.
experiment: Compare Ketamine, memantine and d-APV in the same slice model with a time-matched control. Measure receptor inhibition, burst frequency, sag and activity after washout.

chapters.title: The WWOX finding
chapters.takeaway: One preparation establishes that NMDA receptor activation matters for these bursts. It leaves open what initiated the bursts and whether a pore blocker reproduces the effect.

rows: Spontaneous bursts
36/42 neuronal Wwox-knockout slices, 4/23 heterozygous slices, 0/11 wild-type slices
Cortical slices at postnatal days 13–17. Slices and bursts are nested within animals.
d-APV
Abolished bursts in five slices from three knockout animals
Competitive antagonist. Ketamine and memantine were not tested.
Carbenoxolone
Reported 87% lower frequency and no reversal after washout
Nonselective; a pannexin blocker failed to reproduce the effect. The paper’s duration and amplitude descriptions differ from the figure.
d-APV washout
Frequency bar about 1.8× baseline by image reading
The error bar includes baseline. The text describes recovery. Rebound remains unproven.

sections.label: Data / Evidence
paragraphs: The published electrophysiology points to neocortical hyperexcitability, smaller spontaneous inhibitory currents and increased sag. The separate Wwox studies that used ketamine for anaesthesia supplied no controlled seizure endpoint for ketamine.

sections.label: Inference
paragraphs: A regenerative burst can depend on NMDA receptors even if a change in inhibition, network drive or intrinsic excitability sets it off. The evidence for pharmacological burst abolition still traces back to one laboratory and one preparation.

chapters.title: Targets, kinetics and exposure
chapters.takeaway: The transfer from d-APV to Ketamine requires two comparisons: receptor action under active conditions and the exposure at which each effect was measured.

rows: NMDA pore block
Ketamine and memantine require channel activity for block and unblock. One culture comparison reported 86% vs 71% trapping.
Assay, Mg²⁺, voltage and subunits affect apparent potency. These fractions were not measured in the Wwox slice.
HCN1 / Ih
Ketamine reduced Ih in cortical pyramidal neurons at a nearby developmental age. The effect disappeared in HCN1-knockout neurons.
Plausible rival if sag and burst frequency change together. Wwox-dependent sensitivity is unknown.
PV interneurons
GluN2A-dependent effects on parvalbumin interneurons were observed in adult visual cortex.
A clue to disinhibition at shallow block. Cell type, age and preparation differ.
Ex vivo transfer
S-ketamine suppressed induced events in adult hippocampal slices without magnesium. The reported bath observation started at 100 µM.
Different preparation. About 11× the highest total human plasma peak in the sources reached, around 8.9 µM.

sections.label: Inference
paragraphs: The pharmacokinetic audit distinguished total plasma, free plasma, CSF, brain and bath exposure. Their relationships were unmeasured in the relevant childhood status epilepticus setting. An observed human peak is neither a clinical target nor a physical ceiling.

sections.label: Hypothesis
paragraphs: Matching evoked NMDA inhibition can separate some alternatives. Residual pore occupancy and the effect of recording probes on untrapping could still make two nominally matched arms behave differently.

chapters.title: Clinical evidence by endpoint
chapters.takeaway: The paediatric literature addresses several different decisions. It cannot be pooled into a WOREE response estimate.

rows: Initial convulsive status epilepticus
Ket-Mid randomised 144 children. Clinical cessation at five minutes: 76% with ketamine plus midazolam, 21% with placebo plus midazolam.
A first-line add-on result in mixed etiologies. Cessation was assessed clinically without EEG confirmation.
Refractory convulsive status epilepticus
KETASER01 stopped at 10 participants; 2/5 in each arm met the study endpoint. Observational series report responses with co-treatment.
Too few randomised data for comparative efficacy. Observational timing and background care limit attribution.
Very young infants
In a three-infant series, seizure resolution and changes in co-infusions were not aligned in a way that isolates ketamine.
A record of treatment experience. It does not support assigning responders to ketamine alone.
Maintenance and development
Memantine trial in mixed DEE lists 9/27 vs 2/27 on a composite crossover outcome. The paired overlap is unavailable to the team.
Trial summaries leave paired significance and harms unresolved. No WOREE developmental benefit established.

sections.label: Inference
paragraphs: The original 24/30 pooled claim and proposed genetically favourable subgroup failed review. An ATP1A2 case supplied concurrent add-on treatment, not a validated ketamine-to-memantine sequence. Other cases used different orders and co-interventions.

sections.label: Data / Evidence depth
paragraphs: The team checked the infant series in full. Full-text routes remained blocked for key memantine, Kuki and Rosati papers. No underlying patient records, treatment plan or timings for individual patients are included here.

chapters.title: Ketamine and recovery after intubation
chapters.takeaway: Functional benefit 6–8 weeks after brief ketamine induction remains undetermined. The closest cohort measured recovery after extubation without an induction comparison.

rows: Mazandi and Loi, neurologic intubations
Ketamine induction in 70/143 children and 495/2,073 registry procedures. Registry adjusted OR for the acute adverse-event composite was 1.34 (95% CI, 0.99–1.81).
Peri-intubation. Clinical selection and other sedatives. No later function estimate.
Bhutta, 24 cardiac surgery infants
Single pre-bypass administration, 13 vs 11 randomized. No statistically detected pre/post Bayley-II difference in the abstract.
At 2–3 weeks. Small surgical pilot.
Jacobwitz, 69 children and neonates with status epilepticus
cEEG seizure cessation 32/69 and reduction 19/69. Median infusion 85.7 hours. 66/69 intubated before exposure.
Acute response with prior therapy, no control. Variable discharge timing.
Othman, 144 children with convulsive status
Ketamine added to midazolam. Clinical cessation 55/72 vs 15/72 at 5 min and seizure control 57/72 vs 48/72 at 24 h.
No EEG confirmation. Rescue treatment allowed. Follow-up ended at 24 h.
Mason and Curley, dexmedetomidine

Paired EEG in 16 children found more interictal spikes during sedation. A multi-drug strategy including dexmedetomidine was associated with a 4.1-point higher estimated IQ than opioid and benzodiazepine only.
During sedation vs cognition years later after multiday exposure. No class randomization in the IQ analysis.
Chamberlain, 310 randomized in emergency care
Lorazepam vs diazepam: clinical seizure cessation 97/133 vs 101/140. Sedation 66.9% vs 50%.
Clinical seizure assessment at 10–30 min. Respiratory safety and sedation were assessed over 4 h. Follow-up function was unmeasured.
Bhalala, 35 selected PICU patients
Propofol bridge lasted a median 7 h 54 min. 34/35 remained extubated at 24 h. 34/35 received dexmedetomidine and 32/35 lorazepam during admission.
Peri-extubation physiology. Patients were selected for planned extubation, without a control group and with substantial coexposure.
Maddux, 144 ventilated survivors
102 regained pre-illness quality-of-life threshold, at a median 52 days after extubation (IQR 9.4–113.4). 39/102 had a later decline.
Conditional on recovery. No induction comparison. Quality-of-life threshold and gain above baseline are distinct outcomes.
MacDonald, 150 PICU survivors
At two months after PICU discharge, physical PedsQL was at least one standard deviation below the study reference in 30/82 assessed after invasive ventilation.
The group reference does not account for premorbid function, and the comparison did not identify induction medication. Baseline case mix differed substantially across types of respiratory support.

sections.label: Data and inference
paragraphs: The acute ketamine signal and post-PICU recovery are supported by different cohorts. The official labels describe ketamine redistribution and active norketamine, age-dependent dexmedetomidine exposure, longer lorazepam sedation and propofol recovery dependent on infusion duration. Persistent change at seven weeks would require evidence of an intermediate mechanism. Acute salivation and later secretion management require separate measurements.

sections.label: Hypothesis and discriminating comparison
paragraphs: An induction effect could alter the early seizure or cardiorespiratory burden and thereby influence recovery. Compare existing induction strategies at the same pre-intubation severity and premorbid function. Separate subsequent sedatives and antiseizure medication changes. Measure acute EEG seizure burden, arousal, interaction, motor function and airway secretion management separately. Assess infection resolution, ventilatory support and rehabilitation by their timing. Compare domain change at 42–56 days from intubation, with death and follow-up losses reported.

sections.label: Decision and WWOX transfer
paragraphs: Public RESTORE metadata identify intubation timing, baseline function, ketamine-use fields and a published six-month functional endpoint. The inspected fields do not establish an induction-only contrast with a week-seven measurement. Find a source with that joint coverage before estimating a drug effect. The WWOX slice observation supports an acute NMDA-dependent circuit comparison and cannot establish human developmental or recovery outcomes.

chapters.title: Comparators and safety
chapters.takeaway: Evidence changes with the endpoint, age, exposure duration and comparator. The strongest alternative for a clinical syndrome may answer a different question from the best preclinical probe.

rows: Ketamine and memantine
Ketamine has more direct acute-status evidence; memantine is a useful pore-blocker comparator. Other NMDA agents offer narrower mechanistic probes.
None of these comparisons demonstrates a disease-specific benefit.
Lithium and ethosuximide
Both have one in vivo global-Wwox-null provoked-seizure experiment. Lithium also showed an effect in wild type.
No treatment-by-genotype test. Different endpoint and preparation from the Ketamine question.
Other syndrome-specific approaches
Controlled trials exist in other paediatric disorders for established medicines or dietary approaches.
Direct comparison requires a matched syndrome, seizure type, endpoint and developmental context.
Short vs prolonged exposure
The safety audit separated procedural sedation, intensive-care series, neonatal animal studies and case reports.
Prolonged exposure and long-term development in infants with WOREE remain unmeasured.

sections.label: Data / Evidence
paragraphs: Published reports include electrographic seizure provocation, haemodynamic and airway events. Hepatobiliary and urinary events with prolonged or repeated use are mainly case or intensive-care evidence. Incidence from brief procedural sedation cannot be moved to prolonged exposure.

sections.label: Limits for WOREE
paragraphs: The laboratory also checked glucose, retinal and optic phenotypes. Ocular effects such as nystagmus and raised intraocular pressure have been recorded outside WOREE. The available literature could not quantify genotype-specific metabolic or optic risk.

chapters.title: Follow-up comparisons
chapters.takeaway: After the Ketamine review, the team explored alternative agents and the measurements that would let their effects be compared fairly.

rows: Vigabatrin case audit
Exposure recorded in 22 children across 10 reports. Response stated for 11, of whom eight had qualified reports of response. Co-treatment and missing outcomes limit attribution.
Syndrome and age-specific measures, with ocular risk and existing optic involvement considered separately.
Age and seizure type
Young-rodent data showed that a compound can suppress generalised events while increasing smaller events. Much of the evidence came from rat studies and related reports.
Prespecify age, seizure types and EEG or behavioural endpoints. Track motor impairment separately from seizure scores.
T-type calcium currents
Lithium and Ethosuximide provided in vivo provocation comparators. The T-type mechanism of Ethosuximide remained unresolved.
Measure current and exposure in the relevant preparation before assigning a CaV3 mechanism.
Chloride and GABA
The chloride audit identified a missing Wwox-specific measurement upstream of several proposed agents. NKCC1 and KCC2 evidence transfers from other settings.
Establish how GABA acts in the selected Wwox model and age range before prioritising chloride-directed interventions.

sections.label: Inference
paragraphs: The more informative comparisons follow the question: acute rescue, spontaneous burden, induced seizure threshold, developmental outcomes or tolerability. The laboratory found no single compound that led on all of them.

chapters.title: Independent review
chapters.takeaway: The audit strengthened the case for a narrowly defined mechanistic comparison and removed several claims that had made the drug look more specific than the data justified.

rows: Unique mechanism match
Overstated. d-APV was the slice reagent. The relevant experimental evidence has one origin.
A pore-blocker result is still needed.
Pathway coverage percentages
Arithmetic reproduced under the source graph; estimates changed when node definitions and the denominator changed.
A graph-coverage score does not measure drug activity or predicted benefit.
GSK3β duration switch
Only two of nine initial labels matched the paper in one audit. Stress model, age, exposure and measurement differed.
The apparent short-versus-long reversal did not survive. A signalling change cannot by itself establish clinical harm or benefit.
Developmental collision and chronic maintenance
Other-species and other-disorder signals kept as transfers. The memantine crossover and ATP1A2 sequence had unresolved attribution.
No comparative superiority claim and no patient-treatment sequence follow.

sections.label: Data / Evidence
paragraphs: Checks included the source identifiers and quotations, independent appraisal of the cell and animal work, re-reading figures, verification of the pharmacokinetic arithmetic and comparisons by endpoint. Many citations existed and quotations matched while their original interpretation needed correction.
The audit found all 25 cited PMIDs and matched 23 of 24 quotations. Those checks were kept separate from judging what each citation actually supported.

sections.label: Inference
paragraphs: The model without slow adaptation returned to baseline and missed the reported washout overshoot. A slow-adaptation model can generate rebound by construction. Scenario weights and simulated outcomes are exploratory, with no validated predictive probability.

chapters.title: Decisive experiments
chapters.takeaway: The team’s most informative follow-up is a comparison in the same cortical preparation, with interpretation specified before observing the outcome.

columns: What would make it more credible
rows: A pore-blocker class effect
Both pore blockers suppress bursts at comparable evoked NMDA block, with recovery tracked beside d-APV and vehicle.
Both fail at verified depth while d-APV reproduces its effect in the same preparation. One failed agent only weakens that agent.
Ketamine-specific route
Ketamine differs from memantine at the same evoked depth and the difference tracks sag or another independent readout.
The agents converge and sag does not distinguish them. Different trapping or effective block must still be considered.
Withdrawal rebound or persistent suppression
Time course after washout differs from a time-matched control and can be related to recovery of receptor function.
Apparent persistence disappears as receptor occupancy recovers or falls within time-matched variability.

sections.label: Experiment
paragraphs: The proposed preclinical set uses d-APV as a reference and Ketamine and memantine as pore-blocker comparators, with vehicle. Record burst rate, evoked inhibition, Ih sag and early and later washout in the same preparation. Record the probe schedule because channel opening can release a trapped drug. Animal-level replication and a reproducible baseline are required for interpretation.

sections.label: Decision boundary
paragraphs: A reproducible, well-controlled result in that preparation would justify asking whether spontaneous activity in an intact model changes. It would leave efficacy, development and safety in children open. GluN2B-selective modulation is a further mechanistic question with its own comparator.
